model_output.verdict: A store manager with strong results at one location and a second turnaround that needs an explanation.
write_up: A recruiter sees a retail manager running a $9.4M store, with sales growth, lower turnover and less shrink. The headline claims two store turnarounds, but the work below only shows what changed at one.
The fixed-schedule line is the model: it names the change you made and gives the turnover figures on both sides. Add the story behind the other turnaround, and the headline has something to stand on.

cards.line: Retail store manager who has turned around two underperforming stores in a 60-store regional chain.
cards.cannot_tell: The results below show what changed at your current store, but not what happened at the other one. A recruiter will look for both stories after reading this claim.
cards.example: Retail store manager who has turned around two underperforming stores in a 60-store regional chain; at the other store, [what you changed and what happened]
cards.question: What did you change at the other store, and what happened there?

cards.line: - Cut annual staff turnover from 68% to 41% by moving to fixed weekly schedules
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as your model. A recruiter can see both your decision and the movement in a measure that matters for a store.

fit.note: Your experience points toward store management, with earlier assistant manager and department supervisor work. The current role makes your management responsibilities and store results easy to see.
